AcpAgentProbe.description:
Combined result of probing an ACP agent (Settings → "Detect models"): the
model selector, the session-mode selector, and every other config option the
agent advertises, discovered from one throwaway `session/new` so the agent
process is spawned only once (issue #607).

configOptions.description:
Every `select` config option the agent advertised, including the model one.
Cached on the agent config as {@link AcpAgentConfig.availableConfigOptions}
so the composer picker can offer reasoning level / mode without re-spawning
the agent.

models.description: The agent's model selector, or `null` when it exposes no selectable models.

modes.description: The agent's session-mode selector, or `null` when it exposes no modes.

AcpAutoSetupResult.description: Outcome of the one-shot ACP preset auto-setup (install/register/detect).

failed.description: Presets that could not be set up, with a short reason.

installed.description: Preset ids whose npm adapter was installed via Socket Firewall.

modelsDetected.description: Preset ids whose models were detected and cached.

registered.description: Preset ids newly registered as usable agents.

upgraded.description:
Preset ids whose already-installed npm adapter was upgraded to the registry
latest (same Socket-Firewall path as a fresh install).

AcpConfigCategory.description:
Semantic category ACP attaches to a session config option. The spec reserves
the un-prefixed names below and is explicit that the field is a **UX hint**:
"It MUST NOT be required for correctness. Clients MUST handle missing or
unknown categories gracefully." So Copse renders every advertised option
regardless, and uses the category only to label and place it —
{@link ACP_OTHER_CATEGORY } stands in for absent/unknown/vendor (`_`-prefixed)
values.

AcpConfigChoice.description: A selectable value of an ACP config option (`SessionConfigValueId` + label).

AcpConfigOption.description:
One `select`-kind ACP session config option, flattened from a `session/new`
response. This is the generic form of {@link AcpModelSelector}: the model
picker is just the `category: "model"` instance of it, and reasoning level
(`thought_level`) and permission mode (`mode`) arrive the same way.

currentValue.description: The value the agent starts a session on when Copse selects nothing.

description.description: Optional agent-provided description of what the option does.

AcpModeChoice.description: A selectable session-mode id + label, from an ACP `SessionMode` (issue #607).

description.description: Optional agent-provided description of what the mode does.

AcpModeSelector.description:
An external ACP agent's session-mode selector, discovered from a `session/new`
response (its `modes` state). Surfaced to the settings picker so the user can
choose a permission mode to persist on the agent config (issue #607).

choices.description: The modes the agent can operate in.

currentValue.description: The mode the agent starts a session in when none is selected.

AcpModelChoice.description: A selectable model value + label, flattened from an ACP model config option.

description.description:
Optional agent-provided description of the model. Agents that label their
models by family alone put the version here (Claude Code: label "Sonnet",
description "Sonnet 5 · Efficient for routine tasks"), so the picker folds
it back into the row — see `acpModelChoiceLabel`.

AcpModelSelector.description:
An external ACP agent's model selector, discovered from a `session/new`
response (its `category: "model"` config option). Surfaced to the settings
picker so the user can choose a model to persist on the agent config.

currentValue.description: The model the agent starts a session on when none is selected.

AgentContainer.description: Which dot-container a definition came from; decides the filename-`name` rule.

AgentRunPayload.description:
The JSON payload a host serializes into an agent run's prompt. Parsed back by
`parseAgentRunPayload` — the loop's run input, so the shape lives with the loop.

continuationBudgetUsed.description:
Machine turns already spent in this turn tree before this run (decision 5).
The renderer counts queue-drain continuations (hook send-now, stop / subagent
follow-ups); the run seeds the shared ledger with it so its in-run
tighteners (closeout / pre-review / remediation) share one counter per turn
tree rather than restarting the budget each run.

invokedAgent.description: Subagent the user invoked with `/name` this turn.

model.description: Per-thread model override; absent means "use the global default setting".

reasoning.description:
Per-chat reasoning dial for this turn, from the composer footer. Overrides
the level saved against the model in Settings; absent means that level
applies.

turnTreeId.description:
Turn-tree epoch this run belongs to (decision 16 / C3). Minted by the
renderer for a human submission / release and carried on every dispatch of
the turn tree (the initial run and each queue-drained continuation), so the
main-process continuation ledger keys the same per-turn-tree counter the
renderer's drain-time budget check uses. Absent → the run falls back to the
thread id as its turn-tree key.

workingBrief.description: Thread working brief captured in renderer store before the run.

AgentSource.description: Where a definition was found. `project` and `plugin` are untrusted authors.

agentPath.description: Absolute path to the definition file.

unsupportedFields.description: Frontmatter fields recognised but not yet honoured.

name.description: Original file name, shown on the composer chip and in the prompt note.

path.description: Absolute path of the stored copy, inside the thread's blobs directory.

maxLiveWorktrees.description: Maximum unresolved linked checkouts this schedule may retain. Defaults to 1.

AutomationScheduleInput.description: Editable fields accepted by create/update IPC. Project ownership is separate.

coalescedReason.description: Why a fresh task could not safely start. Present only when coalesced.

disposition.description: Whether this trigger started a turn or found the schedule's prior turn still active.

CanvasArtefact.description:
A renderable artefact produced by an MCP-UI resource (the "canvas").
Currently only self-contained HTML (`text/html`) is rendered; the type carries
the mime so future kinds (e.g. `text/uri-list`) can branch on it.

body.description: The artefact body: an HTML document, or a URL for `text/uri-list`.

preview.description:
A small PNG `data:` URL of the rendered artefact, captured from the agent
browser session. Absent when the canvas could not be mirrored (no Electron
platform, tab limit reached, capture failed) — every consumer must treat a
missing preview as normal and simply show no thumbnail.

sourcePath.description:
Workspace-relative path of the file the artefact was rendered from, when it
came from one (`render_html_artefact`'s preferred `path` argument). Absent
for inline HTML and for external MCP servers, which have no such file.

Provenance, and the reason a restored artefact can show later edits: when
the canvas store reopens a saved artefact it prefers this file over its own
snapshot, so editing the HTML and reopening shows the edit.

threadId.description: Thread that rendered this artefact; scopes tabs and previews with common titles.

title.description: Friendly title shown on the canvas tab (falls back to the resource URI).

CanvasArtefactIdentity.description: Identity used when promoting a rendered artefact into the visible pane.

CanvasArtefactReference.description:
A canvas artefact attached to one assistant message for transcript display.
The owning message already supplies the thread scope, so persisting the title
alone avoids baking a stale thread id into forks or imported transcripts.

CanvasArtefactSummary.description:
A saved artefact as the transcript needs it: enough to draw the preview card
that offers to reopen it, without reading the (much larger) body back.

ContextBreakdown.description:
Estimated token cost of everything that would be sent on the next prompt,
split into named parts. Computed before sending so the composer can show
what the default context costs and how the draft message adds to it.

ContextBreakdownSegment.description: One slice of the pre-send context estimate (e.g. system prompt, tools, your message).

ContextSegmentKey.description: Which part of the assembled prompt a breakdown segment represents.

ContextSnapshot.description: Live context fill snapshot (updated during an agent run).

source.description: Present when the context owner reported this snapshot directly.

CuratedMcpServerStatus.description: A curated catalog entry joined with its enabled flag and live connection state.

description.description: One-line description of what the server provides.

enabled.description: Whether the user has turned this server on (off by default).

name.description: Stable id, also used as the server name and `mcp__<name>__` tool prefix.

CursorPluginSummary.description: Summary of a Cursor plugin discovered on disk (skills + optional MCP).

mcpConfigPath.description: Resolved MCP config file path, when `mcpServers` is set in the manifest.

name.description: Plugin id from `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` `name`, or the directory basename.

root.description: Absolute path to the plugin root (directory containing `.cursor-plugin/`).

CursorRuleKind.description:
Cursor project-rule activation kinds (issue #636). Mirrors Cursor's four
`.mdc` rule types: Always / Auto-Attached / Agent-Requested / Manual.

CursorRuleSummary.description: Summary of a discovered `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (or legacy `.cursorrules`) entry.

bytes.description: Byte length of the rule body (frontmatter stripped).

name.description: Path relative to the workspace root (e.g. `.cursor/rules/style.mdc`).

path.description: Absolute path of the rule file.

DebugTraceArchiveExport.description: Archive bytes plus the Copse build that interpreted and exported the trace.

DebugTraceBuildInfo.description: Build provenance captured alongside the archive used by Debug trace.

DecisionEvent.description: One line of the durable decision audit (thread spine `type: "decision"`).

at.description: Epoch milliseconds, assigned by the writer.

cause.description:
Why the user was interrupted, for a decision that prompted. Absent on
non-interactive verdicts and on prompts recorded before the taxonomy
existed — `summarizePromptCauses` counts those separately rather than
guessing. An unrecognised value is dropped at parse time, so a log written
by a newer build degrades to "uncaused" here instead of failing to load.

confidence.description: Classifier confidence in [0, 1], when the actor is a classifier.

id.description: Opaque unique id (uuid), assigned by the writer.

kind.description:
Decision domain, e.g. `shell` | `mcp` | `web` | `pii` | `browser` |
`github-write` | `custom-tool` | `port-binding` | `model-compare` | `acp` |
`install` | `classification` | `hook`. A free string so new gates need no
schema bump; consumers should treat unknown kinds gracefully.

remembered.description: Whether the grant was made sticky (the "remember" checkbox).

scope.description: Scope the decision applied at / granted, e.g. `sandbox` | `external`.

source.description: Redacted extra context: hook config path, classifier model id, etc.

subject.description: Redacted subject the decision was about: a command, tool name, or origin.

threadId.description: Originating thread id (links back to the spine), when known.

toolCallId.description: Tool call this decision authorized, when known.

DecisionVerdict.description:
The outcome. `approved`/`denied` are user verdicts; `allowed`/`blocked`/`ask`
are non-interactive policy/hook verdicts; `timeout` is a prompt that expired
unanswered (treated as a denial by the caller, recorded distinctly here);
`deferred` is a prompt an unattended run queued for later review instead of
showing — the action did not run, and a separate line records the human's
eventual answer.

DeclaredMcpServer.description:
An MCP server a plugin's `mcp.json` declares that the app is **not** running.

An installed plugin can name servers Copse never spawns — because the plugin
is turned off, or because its declarations are validated but not yet wired
into the agent loop. Left out of Settings entirely, those declarations are
invisible: the list would say "no servers" while a package on disk names
three. Since the point of this section is to be the complete account of the
app's outbound connections, a declaration that is not running is still
something to show — as a distinct, inert row, never mixed in with the live
ones.

pluginEnabled.description: Whether the declaring plugin is currently enabled.

pluginId.description: Registry id of the plugin that declares it — also what Settings shows.

reason.description: Why it is not running, in one phrase.

DetectedAcpAgent.description: A {@link KnownAcpAgent} annotated with what was found on the device.

args.description: Arguments that put the command into ACP mode.

autoInstall.description:
Whether auto-setup may install {@link installPackage} for the user (through
Socket Firewall) when {@link requiresClient} is present but the agent isn't.
Only true for npm-distributed agents; never for `curl | bash` installers.

command.description: Executable that speaks ACP over stdio (looked up on PATH).

docsUrl.description: Where to read more about the agent.

envHints.description: Environment variables the agent typically needs (names only; values are the user's).

id.description: Slug used as the configured agent id and the `acp:<id>` model value.

install.description: Shell command that installs the agent binary (e.g. an `npm install -g …`).

installPackage.description:
npm package spec to install for auto-setup (Socket-Firewall-wrapped). Present
only for agents distributed on npm; absent for script-installed binaries such
as `cursor-agent` (which auto-setup will never install — see {@link autoInstall}).

note.description: Short note shown by the detector (auth, caveats).

path.description: Absolute path the command resolves to, when installed.

preset.description:
Whether auto-setup should register this agent as a ready-to-use preset once
its binary is available. Curated to one adapter per client (Claude, Cursor)
so auto-setup doesn't register several near-duplicate entries.

reauth.description:
Shell command that refreshes an *existing but expired* sign-in. Distinct from
{@link setup}: minting a fresh long-lived token (`claude setup-token`) is the
first-run path, while an expired OAuth session is fixed by signing in again
(`claude /login`). Falls back to {@link setup} when absent — see
`acpReauthCommand`.

requiresClient.description:
Parent client whose presence gates this agent in auto-setup. For the Claude
adapter it's `claude` (installing the ACP SDK only makes sense when the user
has Claude); for Cursor it's the `cursor-agent` binary itself. Absent = no gate.

running.description: A process whose argv[0] is this command is currently running.

sandbox.description:
Seatbelt confinement preset (issue #590): domains the agent's process may
reach and the home-relative dirs it needs for its own config/state. Copied
onto the registered `AcpAgentConfig`; agents without a preset spawn
unsandboxed. Keep domains minimal — the user can widen them per agent.

sandboxedPermissionMode.description:
ACP **session mode** (`SessionModeId`) to default the agent into when it
spawns **sandboxed** and the user hasn't chosen one (issue #607). The
seatbelt already contains writes to the workspace/scratch and the post-turn
audit surfaces anything that bypassed the diff queue, so prompt-per-edit
adds friction without adding safety — the Claude adapters default to
`acceptEdits`. A user-set `permissionMode` always wins; unsandboxed agents
keep their own default prompting regardless. The apply step still guards
that the agent actually advertises this mode, so a stale value is harmless.

setup.description: Shell command that authenticates the agent / mints a token (e.g. `claude setup-token`).

title.description: Human-readable name for the picker / detector output.

DetectedEnvKey.description: A provider API key discovered in the environment, masked for display.

alreadyConfigured.description: Whether a key for this provider is already saved in Settings.

envVar.description: The environment variable it was read from (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).

masked.description: Masked preview of the key — the raw value never crosses IPC.

source.description: Where it was found: `environment` or a shell file label (e.g. `~/.zshrc`).

ExternalEditor.description: One installed editor as surfaced to the renderer dropdown.

ExternalEditorList.description: Result of `editors:list`: installed editors plus the sticky default.

lastUsedId.description: Editor last launched from this app, when it is still installed.

ExtraProvider.description:
An effective provider: the schema-derived preset shape (see
provider-metadata.ts for per-field docs) plus the fields derived here.

apiStyle.description: Wire protocol. Absent means Chat Completions.

baseUrl.description:
OpenAI-compatible base URL the SDK talks to. Held to the same floor as
user-added customs (`isSafeCredentialBaseUrl`): https only — no embedded
credentials, no private/link-local hosts — except http to loopback for
the local-server presets. Enforced here, not in a test, because a preset
host is credential-egress-allowlisted without a prompt.

builtin.description: True for a shipped preset (locked label/base URL, env-var fallback).

envVar.description: Env var that can also supply the key.

extraBody.description: Extra fields merged into every request body.

fallbackContextWindow.description: Always resolved: the catalog value or DEFAULT_EXTRA_PROVIDER_CONTEXT.

id.description: Stable slug: model-selection prefix source and API-key lookup id.

keyPrefix.description: Key-format prefix, checked before any network call.

local.description:
True when the base URL is a loopback/local server. Local providers render in
Settings → Local models (not the cloud Providers panel) and are usable
without an API key. Derived from the base URL via `isLocalBaseUrl`.

models.description: Curated/known model shortlist for the picker (may be empty for a fresh custom).

ExtraProviderModel.description:
A preset/custom model entry: the schema-derived catalog shape (see
provider-metadata.ts for per-field docs) plus the one computed field.

blendedCostPerMTok.description: 80/20 blended price (0.8 * input + 0.2 * output), pre-calculated for comparison.

contextWindow.description: Context window in tokens; falls back to the provider default.

id.description: Upstream model id sent to the provider.

FollowUpSuggestion.description: A clickable follow-up bubble shown above the input bar.

additions.description: Present when variant is "changes" — rendered as green/red counts.

prompt.description: The message an `action: 'prompt'` bubble sends; absent on action bubbles.

ForkedHistoryResult.description:
How a fork's provider-format history was seeded from the thread it branched
off (`threads:fork`). `copied` is the source sidecar verbatim — the
highest-fidelity result. `rebuilt` was reconstructed from the copied
transcript slice, which cannot carry content that only existed in the run
payload (the fenced blocks inlined for `@`-file / `@`-thread / shell chips).
`empty` means the source had neither recorded provider history nor a visible
transcript that could be rebuilt.

GhIssueSummary.description: An issue in the workspace repo, as listed for roadmap import or review.

body.description: Issue body (truncated by the backend); used to draft a roadmap prompt.

state.description: Present when the backend knows lifecycle state (open listings default to open).

GhPrChecksState.description: Overall CI rollup for a PR head, mirroring github-ci-service's CiOverallState.

autoMergeEnabled.description: True once merge-when-ready / auto-merge has been enabled.

checks.description: Overall CI state, when known from the listing query (else fetched lazily).

isDraft.description: True while the PR is a draft (mark-ready targets this).

afterImage.description: Data URL for the post-change image, when the file is an image.

beforeImage.description: Data URL for the pre-change image, when the file is an image.

deleted.description: The file was deleted in this PR (no `after` content).

directoryFileCount.description: Total untracked files in the directory; may exceed `directoryFiles.length`.

directoryFiles.description:
Present when `path` is an untracked directory: the untracked files inside
it, capped for IPC (a fresh node_modules holds tens of thousands). The
viewer renders these as a file list instead of a text diff.

checks.description: Overall CI state, when known from the listing query (else fetched lazily).

GitBranchInfo.description: Lightweight branch listing: name + most recent commit timestamp.

lastCommitDate.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent commit on this branch.

GitBranchStatus.description: Checked-out branch plus optional open PR (for HEAD or a named branch).

isDirectory.description:
A wholly-untracked directory that `git status` collapsed into a single
`?? dir/` record instead of listing its files. `path` carries no trailing
slash.

GitCommittedChanges.description:
Files changed by commits that have not reached a pull request yet: the
`<base>...HEAD` diff, where `base` is the branch's remote head when an open PR
already carries those commits, and the merge-base with the default branch
otherwise. Committing does not remove work from the Changes panel; it moves
the work into this section.

baseLabel.description: What HEAD was compared against, for display: `main`, `origin/feature-x`.

afterImage.description: Data URL for the post-change image, when the file is an image.

beforeImage.description: Data URL for the pre-change image, when the file is an image.

directoryFileCount.description: Total untracked files in the directory; may exceed `directoryFiles.length`.

directoryFiles.description:
Present when `path` is an untracked directory: the untracked files inside
it, capped for IPC (a fresh node_modules holds tens of thousands). The
viewer renders these as a file list instead of a text diff.

GitHubBackendKind.description: Which backend implementation serviced a GitHub operation.

GitPromptState.description: Repository snapshot captured at a prompt boundary (issue: spine prompt hash / dirty state).

dirty.description: Whether the working tree had staged or unstaged changes at send time.

startingCommit.description: Full HEAD commit SHA the prompt was sent against, or null outside a repo / no commits yet.

agentMessageChars.description: Character count of guidance sent to the agent on deny/ask.

error.description: Error message when a function hook threw (fail-hard, decision 9).

event.description: Canonical or dialect event name that fired (e.g. `stop`, `beforeShellExecution`).

exitCode.description: Process exit code (command hooks); null when killed, absent for function hooks.

hookId.description: Stable hook id: registry id (function hooks) or command string (command hooks).

injectContextChars.description: Character count of injected context (blocking hooks, H2).

nudgeApplied.description: This nudge is the one the loop pushed, not merely one that was offered.

nudgeMechanism.description: How the applied nudge reached the model.

parseOk.description: Whether stdout parsed into a response (command hooks; always true for function hooks).

queuedMessageChars.description: Character count of an async queued follow-up (decision 4).

sandboxBlocked.description: The hook ran inside the project sandbox and was blocked by it (F3, decision 7).

sessionEnvKeys.description: Number of session environment variables exported for later hooks (H4).

updatedInput.description: The hook rewrote the gated tool's input (H1).

userMessageChars.description: Character count of a hook message shown to the user.

HookCardKind.description:
What a hook card is *about* — selects the card's icon + accent:
- `decision`  — a permission verdict (`deny` / `ask`) on a gated action.
- `halt`      — the hook asked to stop the run (`continue: false`, decision 12).
- `execution` — a plain observation / allow run (no blocking verdict).

HookCardStatus.description: Normalized status the card badges + colours by.

HookFamily.description: Which product's on-disk schema produced this hook.

HookQueueMessagePayload.description:
Main → renderer bridge payload for an async hook's `queueMessage` output — the
only async output channel (decision 4). The host translates an async outcome
into this and sends it over `agent:hook_queue_message`; the renderer lands it
in the thread's pending-message queue with origin attribution (decision 10)
and epoch (decision 16). `sendNow` carries byte-for-byte the user's send-now
semantics for a **current** epoch; a stale send-now is downgraded to held on
the renderer side (decision 16) — the staleness check owns the abort back-door.

epoch.description: Emitting turn-tree epoch (decision 16); checked for staleness on arrival.

sendNow.description: Whether the hook requested immediate send (decision 4).

threadId.description: Thread whose queue the message lands in.

HookRunDetail.description:
`hooks:runDetail` result — the raw record behind one hook card, fetched on
demand when the user opens a card's inspector. The transcript holds only the
compact card (decision 10); the bodies live in the thread's blobs, so this is
read straight back off the spine rather than kept in renderer state. Every
field is optional because a run only has the streams its executor produced:
command hooks have stdin/stdout/stderr, function hooks a payload + outcome.

event.description: Canonical or dialect event name that fired.

exitCode.description: Process exit code (command hooks); null when the process was killed.

found.description: False when no `hook_run` with this id is recorded (yet) in the thread.

missing.description:
Refs the record pointed at that are no longer on disk (pruned blobs, or a
run recorded before a capture existed). Named so the inspector can say the
body is gone instead of implying the hook produced nothing.

outcome.description: JSON of the full text of every channel a function hook applied.

payload.description: What the hook was handed: exact stdin JSON (command) / dispatch payload (function).

stdout.description: Raw captured stdout — the response channel (command hooks).

step.description: LLM-call index within the run at emission time (0 = before the first call).

toolset.description: Content-addressed fingerprint of the toolset offered to the model at the time.

turnId.description: Agent run (turn) the execution was attributed to.

HookScope.description: Where a hook definition came from — determines its trust tier.

HookSummary.description: A single discovered hook command for diagnostics / Settings → Sources.

command.description: The shell command Copse will spawn for this hook.

event.description: Lifecycle event name (Cursor or Claude), e.g. `beforeShellExecution` / `PreToolUse`.

lastError.description:
First runtime failure observed this session (crash / timeout / invalid JSON,
**or a blocked-by-sandbox run** — F3, decision 7), surfaced as a per-hook
error indicator. Never affects fail-open semantics.

matcher.description:
Claude matcher group filter (tool-name pattern). Omitted for Cursor hooks and
for Claude groups with no matcher / `"*"`.

sandbox.description:
Whether this hook opted **out** of the project sandbox (Copse `sandbox: false`,
decision 7 / F3). Present and `false` only for the escape — Sources badges it
"outside sandbox" so the risk is visible; omitted means sandboxed-by-default
(the norm, and all Cursor / Claude hooks, which cannot express the escape).

source.description: Absolute path to the config file that declared it.

supported.description:
Whether Copse actually acts on this event. Declared-but-unwired events (e.g.
Cursor `stop`) surface as `false` so Sources can badge them "unsupported"
rather than looking active. Absent means "supported" (back-compat).

HookTestRequest.description:
`hooks:test` request — identify a single discovered hook (as surfaced in
Settings → Sources) to run once against a **synthetic** payload (G2 dry-run
tester). Carries exactly the {@link HookSummary} fields that reconstruct the
hook's spawn (`family` → dialect, `event` → the wire event to synthesize a
payload for, `command`, `source` → the config dir the command resolves
against) plus the `sandbox` escape so the dry run honours F3's
sandboxed-by-default behavior. A dry run never mutates live agent state,
starts a turn, records the spine, or grants a real permission — the returned
{@link BlockingHookOutcome } is *displayed*, never applied.

command.description: The shell command to spawn — the hook's id.

event.description: Dialect wire event name (exactly as shown in Sources / {@link HookSummary.event}).

sandbox.description:
Whether the hook opted out of the project sandbox (Copse `sandbox: false`).
Mirrors {@link HookSummary.sandbox}; absent means sandboxed-by-default.

source.description: Absolute path to the config file that declared it (its dir is the cwd).

HookTestResult.description:
`hooks:test` result — everything one dry run observed. The four raw streams
the tester surfaces (stdin / stdout / stderr / exit / duration) plus the
derived summary (`parseOk`, a one-line `outcomeSummary`). When the hook's
event cannot be synthesized (unsupported / no dialect marshaller), `ran` is
false and `error` explains why — no process was spawned.

canonicalEvent.description: Canonical event the synthetic payload targeted (e.g. `toolGate`).

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the spawned process in milliseconds.

error.description: Why the dry run could not run (unsupported event / missing marshaller); set when `!ran`.

exitCode.description: Process exit code; null when the hook was killed (timeout) or failed to start.

outcomeSummary.description: One-line human-readable summary of the normalized outcome (e.g. `allow`, `deny — <msg>`, `no opinion`).

parseOk.description: Whether the dialect parsed the hook's stdout cleanly.

ran.description: True when a synthetic payload was built and the hook was actually spawned.

sandboxed.description: Whether the hook actually ran inside the project sandbox (macOS-only; a default, not a guarantee).

spawnError.description: True when the process failed to start.

stderr.description: Raw stderr captured from the hook.

stdin.description: The exact JSON string written to the hook's stdin.

stdout.description: Raw stdout captured from the hook (the response channel).

timedOut.description: True when the hook was killed for exceeding the dry-run timeout.

wireEvent.description: The dialect wire event the payload marshalled to (a `toolGate` flavor may differ).

HookValidationWarning.description: A malformed / unrecognised `hooks.json` entry, surfaced as a warning row.

event.description: Event name the bad entry was under, when known.

source.description: Absolute path to the config file that declared it.

HooksListResult.description: `hooks:list` payload: the discovered hooks plus any authoring-time warnings.

reason.description: Human-readable scale-guard / skip reason. Present for `limited` / `skipped`.

startedAt.description: Epoch ms when the oldest still-running build started. Present while `building`.

IndexPhase.description:
Workspace indexing status surfaced to the renderer (footer indicator).

Two components are tracked independently: the in-memory file-path index
(fast — seconds) and the semantic symbol index (gortex/vera — can run for
minutes on a cold repo, #517). `building` means at least one build/update
pass is currently running for that component.

`limited` / `skipped` are scale-guard outcomes (#795): text/regex search
stays available while semantic indexing (and recursive watching) refuse to
start unbounded work on oversized umbrella workspaces. They are not errors.

InstructionScope.description: Where an instruction file lives: user-global or project/workspace-scoped.

KnowledgeNote.description:
A single knowledge note. `body` is the prose (a memory's content, a roadmap
item's prompt); `fields` holds type-specific scalar frontmatter (e.g. a roadmap
note's `notes`).

fields.description: Extra type-specific scalar frontmatter, round-tripped verbatim.

file.description: Absolute path of the backing OKF markdown file.

status.description: Type-specific lifecycle status, or null when the type has none.

MachineMessageOrigin.description: Provenance for a host-native continuation that started without a human submit.

operationId.description: Durable background/supervisor operation that requested the continuation.

McpServerOrigin.description:
Where a server's definition came from.

Settings → MCP servers is the one place that answers "what is this app
allowed to talk to, and who asked for it". `source` alone cannot: it is a
bare path, and telling `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (the user's own) apart from a
plugin's bundled `mcp.json` means knowing where each root lives — knowledge
the main process has and the renderer does not. So the origin is classified
where it is knowable and shipped alongside the path.

configDisabled.description: `"disabled": true` in the on-disk MCP config; cannot be enabled from the UI.

curated.description: Defined by the built-in "Copse reviewed" catalog rather than an mcp.json file.

originDetail.description: Human label for the origin — a plugin's name, a config filename.

tools.description: Human tool names (without the mcp__server__ prefix).

userEnabled.description: User has not turned this server off in Settings (app-local override).

attachments.description: Display-only attachment chips for user messages (see {@link TranscriptAttachment}).

canvasArtefacts.description: Canvas previews presented with this answer without fabricating tool calls.

commandSummary.description: Small-model rollup label for this message's batch of shell commands.

hookCards.description:
Hook cards (executions / deny-ask decisions / halts) that fired during this
message's turn (decision 10). **Display-only and derived** — populated at
fold time from the thread's always-on spine `hook_run` records (decision 6)
and appended live from the `hook_run` stream chunk. Never persisted via the
message explode path: the spine's `hook_run` lines are the single source of
truth, so this resolves purely from spine data (decision 17), never from live
hook registration.

images.description: Pasted image attachments as data URLs (user messages only).

model.description:
Primary-chat model that produced this assistant message — the concrete
route actually run, after a dynamic selector (`auto:…`) was expanded.
Surfaced in the transcript only when the thread used more than one primary
model — subagent models live on {@link SubagentSession.model }.

origin.description:
Provenance when this turn was started without a human submit. The
message role stays `user` for the LLM; `origin` lives purely in the data
model so the transcript can mark a hook-originated turn (a hook send-now /
`stop`-follow-up that dispatched). Carried through the spine so the marker
survives a reload (history stays honest about authorship). `editedByUser`
flips `true` once a human edits a hook-queued message before it dispatches.

reasoning.description:
Accumulated reasoning / "thinking" text streamed before the answer, shown in
a collapsible disclosure. Never sent back upstream as conversation history.

requestedModel.description:
The model the user asked for for this turn — the picker/requested
selection, which may be a dynamic selector (`auto:…`) rather than a
concrete route. The resolved route the turn actually ran on lives on
{@link Message.model}. Absent on messages written before this was captured.

startingCommit.description:
Repository state this prompt started from (user messages only), captured at
send time. `startingCommit` is the HEAD SHA the turn began on; `dirty`
records whether the working tree had uncommitted changes at that moment.
Best-effort: absent outside a git repo, or for messages sent through a path
that doesn't capture it (e.g. resend).

toolSummary.description:
Small-model polish for the turn's tool rollup (`.tool-card-rollup`). The
deterministic canned label shows immediately; this replaces it when ready
and never blocks delivery.

asOf.description:
ISO date the link was last reviewed. Absent on a card derived at lookup
time from the model id itself (see `huggingFaceCardUrl`), which is as
current as the id is.

url.description: The vendor's own published page or PDF.

ModelCardKind.description: Whether a link is a card about this model, or a vendor hub listing cards.

ModelCardOrigin.description: How a candidate URL was arrived at. Decides ordering and how it is labelled.

ModelComparison.description:
Result of running the working-diff review through two models and a judge that
compares their findings (the "model comparison harness"). `reviewA`/`reviewB`
are each model's independent verdict; `synthesis` is the judge's comparison
(agreements, disagreements, unique catches, overall recommendation).

cost.description: Human-readable cost estimate for the whole run (e.g. `~$0.04`).

models.description: Model ids used for the two reviews (a, b) and the judge synthesis.

synthesis.description: The judge's comparison of the two verdicts.

ModelParameters.description:
User-chosen generation parameters for one model selection. Every field is
optional and an absent field means "send nothing" — the provider default,
not a value of our choosing. That distinction matters: a model's own default
temperature is not necessarily 1, and sending 1 is not the same as omitting.

maxOutputTokens.description: User-selected per-response ceiling for OpenAI-compatible transports.

cacheCreationPricePerMTok.description: USD per million cache-write input tokens; falls back to the input rate.

cacheReadPricePerMTok.description: USD per million cache-read input tokens; falls back to the input rate.

ModelPricingMap.description: `model selection → pricing`, keyed exactly as the usage ledger records models.

ModelSelectionEvent.description: Durable attribution for one committed thread-model selection.

cacheCreationTokens.description:
Portion of `inputTokens` written to the provider prompt cache (Anthropic
`cache_creation_input_tokens`).

cacheReadTokens.description:
Portion of `inputTokens` served from the provider prompt cache (Anthropic
`cache_read_input_tokens`). Billed far cheaper than fresh input; absent for
providers/usage that don't report cache stats.

estimatedTokens.description: Some contributing events used estimated (not agent-reported) token counts.

pricingKnown.description: True for catalogued routes, including routes whose published rate is zero.

OrphanProjectStore.description:
A thread-store directory under `~/.copse/workspace/<id>/` that has no matching
project entry in config — threads that would otherwise be invisible. Surfaced
so they can be re-attached to a folder rather than recovered by hand (#997).

id.description: The store directory id (also the project id it would re-attach under).

threadCount.description: How many thread directories the store holds.

PanelBadge.description: A short label displayed on a row / node (e.g. "local", "shell").

kind.description: Stable id for the badge kind, used to pick a style.

label.description: Human text — the badge shows this verbatim.

PanelData.description:
The payload one `panel_update` chunk carries. A plugin emits this whenever its
panel data changes; each update **replaces** the panel's contents (same
"whole plan per update" model ACP `plan` uses), which keeps the renderer's
update path trivial and matches the todo panel today.

PanelEntry.description:
One entry in a level-2 panel. Both list rows and tree nodes share this shape
— a tree node adds `children`. `id` is stable across updates so a renderer
can key on it, mirroring how ACP plan entries need stable indices to update
(`session-update-adapter.ts`'s `acp-plan-<n>` ids).

badges.description: Zero or more short labels rendered inline with the row.

status.description: Optional lifecycle status (drives the row icon + a11y state).

PanelListData.description: An ordered list panel — the ACP-`plan` shape (list of {@link PanelEntry}).

title.description: Optional header shown above the rows.

PanelTreeNode.description:
A tree node — a {@link PanelEntry} that can nest. Nesting is intentionally
unbounded in the type; a renderer may cap depth for layout, but the data
model doesn't (Sources panel–style trees can be deep).

badges.description: Zero or more short labels rendered inline with the row.

status.description: Optional lifecycle status (drives the row icon + a11y state).

PlanCreditGrant.description: Account credit grant reported alongside a provider's subscription limits.

remainingCents.description: Credit still available, in USD cents.

totalCents.description: Original credit grant value, in USD cents.

usedCents.description: Credit already consumed, in USD cents.

label.description: Short label for the inferred tier (`Pro`, `Max 5x`, …).

PlanProviderId.description: Shared types for subscription plan-usage windows (Claude / Codex / HF / Cursor).

error.description: Fatal snapshot-level failure before provider-specific checks could finish.

PlanWindow.description: One rolling (or fixed) usage window reported by a provider.

limitDollars.description:
API-equivalent dollar cap for this window, when the provider reports it
(Claude legacy `limit_dollars` / `spend` money).

resetsAt.description: ISO-8601 reset time when known; `null` when the provider omits it.

severity.description:
Provider urgency hint when present (`normal` / `warning` / `critical` from
Claude `limits[].severity`). Omitted when the provider does not report it.

unit.description:
How to render absolute used/limit when present. Omit (or `percent`) for
rate-limit bars that are percent-only.

usedCredits.description:
Credits already consumed when {@link unit} is `credits` (Codex
`spend_control`, Claude `extra_usage`).

usedDollars.description:
API-equivalent dollars already consumed in this window, when the provider
reports them (Claude legacy `used_dollars` / `spend` money). Powers
plan-worth-it math; the UI progress bar still uses {@link usedPercent}.

usedPercent.description: Percent of the window already consumed, clamped to `[0, 100]`.

PlanWorthItPayload.description: IPC payload for Settings → Usage plan worth-it card + Expected map mode.

windowExhaustion.description: Exhaustion rates for Claude windows (for the Expected plan map mode).

apiEquivalentBurnPerWeek.description: Mean API-equivalent $ burn over completed weekly windows; null if none.

planFeePerWeek.description: Monthly fee / ~4.348 weeks when a fee is known.

PluginBrowserTabRequest.description: Main → renderer request to create or reveal a visible browser-pane tab.

PluginCapabilitySummary.description:
One named runtime capability a plugin owns — a pure behaviour flag (no tool /
hook / prompt / panel) that any subsystem reads through the registry's
`isCapabilityActive` seam. Enumerated in Settings so the user sees what the
toggle actually gates (e.g. the MCP-UI canvas, the DevTools shortcut).

name.description: Stable capability id read via the registry accessor.

title.description: Human title for the Settings enumeration.

PluginContributionsSummary.description:
Everything a plugin contributes, enumerated for the Settings plugin list. Both
first-party and user plugins surface here (decision 15). Function hooks and
native tool wiring stay on the host side — the renderer only sees ids and
event names it can render.

asyncHooks.description: Async (detached) function hooks the plugin registers.

blockingHooks.description: Blocking (in-loop) function hooks the plugin registers, by canonical event.

browserOrigins.description: Exact origins this plugin may operate in the visible interactive browser pane.

capabilities.description: Named runtime capability flags the plugin owns (pure behaviour, no tool).

commandHooks.description: Command-hook declarations from the manifest (user plugins).

followUps.description: Follow-up bubbles the plugin suggests above the composer while enabled.

mcpServersPath.description: MCP config path a user plugin pulls its tools from (mirrors `plugin.json`).

modelRoutes.description: Thread models contributed by an enabled selected plugin.

permissions.description: Permission / sandbox relaxations the plugin may request while enabled (#1190).

storageNamespace.description: Namespaced storage bag the plugin owns (survives disable — decision 17).

toolNames.description: Native tool names contributed to the model tool list (first-party).

PluginFollowUpSummary.description:
One follow-up bubble a plugin suggests above the composer. `action` and
`when` arrive resolved rather than optional so Settings can show exactly
what a click does and when the bubble appears.

action.description: What the click does — `prompt`, or a first-party host action.

when.description: The workspace condition required before offering it.

PluginPermissionSummary.description:
One permission / sandbox relaxation a plugin DECLARES it may request (issue
#1190) — the authority the plugin opens. The permission-gate only grants a
declared relaxation while the owning plugin is enabled; disabling the plugin
revokes it atomically. Enumerated in Settings so the user sees what a plugin can
request, and exposed for the future install-time capability/permission review
(#1082).

description.description: Optional human description of the authority the relaxation opens.

name.description: Stable relaxation id resolved by the permission-gate.

scope.description: The granularity of the permission grant that gates the relaxation.

title.description: Human title for the Settings enumeration.

PluginPromptBlockSummary.description: One prompt / steering block a plugin contributes (trust framing preserved).

PluginSettingFieldSummary.description: One plugin-scoped setting field, mirrors `PluginSettingField` on the agent side.

default.description: Default value used when nothing is persisted for this plugin + key (a model id for `kind: 'model'`).

id.description: Stable id of the setting, keyed under the plugin's namespace.

options.description: Options for an `enum` field (`kind: 'enum'` only; a `model` field's options are resolved live).

value.description: The current persisted value, or the default when nothing is stored yet.

PluginSettingKind.description:
Kind of value a plugin-scoped setting field carries (rendered generically). Kept
in lockstep with `PluginSettingKind` on the agent side. A `model` field is a
model-id string rendered as the grouped model picker; its option list is the
live model catalogue resolved by the renderer, never shipped in the manifest.

PluginStabilityLevel.description: Product-support status declared by the manifest and shown in Settings.

PluginSummary.description:
One plugin row for the Settings list. `enabled` reflects the shared host
registry's current flag; toggling it in the UI calls `plugins:setEnabled`,
which flips the flag atomically and persists to `electron-store`.

settings.description: Plugin-scoped settings the manifest declares, each carrying its current value.

PluginTrustLevel.description: Trust tier assigned by the host; disk manifests cannot self-promote.

PluginUiContributionSummary.description: One UI contribution enumerated in Settings so the user sees what a plugin adds.

slot.description: Named host slot (level 2 / 3). Absent for level-1 declarative cards.

PluginUiLevel.description: UI contribution levels from the plan (1 = card, 2 = named panel, 3 = real view).

PortOwner.description:
Who owns a Copse-spawned process tree. Only ports whose owning process
descends from one of these are shown as ours (clickable, killable); everything
else (system services, the user's other apps) is inert.

id.description: Terminal session id or background-task id — the handle the UI reveals/kills.

label.description: Human label for the row (shell tab name, or the background command).

PortRow.description: One row in the Ports panel: a listening port plus who (if anyone) owns it.

address.description: Bind address as reported, normalised without brackets (e.g. '0.0.0.0', '127.0.0.1', '::', '::1', '*').

command.description: Best-effort process/command name ('' when the tool doesn't report it).

owner.description: The Shells tab or background task this listener descends from, else null.

pid.description: Owning process id, or null when the tool couldn't attribute one.

port.description: TCP port number bound in LISTEN state.

url.description: Loopback URL to open, or null when the bind address isn't reachable locally.

PortScanResult.description: What the panel renders: the rows, plus whether we could see the host at all.

tool.description: The scan tool that ran, or null when the host has none — see `scanListeningPorts`.

PrActionResult.description:
Result of a PR lifecycle write action (rerun CI, approve, mark-ready,
enable-merge-when-ready). Shared by the main-process backends, the IPC
surface, the agent tools, and the PR pane so all four speak one shape.

message.description: Human-readable summary shown in the PR pane and returned by agent tools.

noop.description: The action left state unchanged because it already held (idempotent no-op).

rerunCount.description: Number of failed workflow runs that were re-run.

strategy.description: Auto-merge strategy chosen from the repo's allowed merge methods.

PreparedThreadCheckout.description: Main-process result of the first-message checkout transaction.

ProjectInstructionSummary.description: Summary of a project instruction file loaded into the system prompt.

active.description: False when discovered but inert (project file in an untrusted workspace).

bytes.description: Byte length of the trimmed content fed to the prompt.

path.description: Absolute path of the file on disk.

plan.description: Plan name when the provider reports one (`Max 5x`, `plus`, …).

QueuedMessageOrigin.description:
Provenance of a queued message (decision 10). A queued message can be authored
by a human (origin absent) or produced by an async hook's `queueMessage`
output — the only async output channel (decision 4). The message role stays
`user` for the LLM; `origin` lives purely in the data model so the UI can
attribute it and the spine stays honest about authorship.

event.description: Canonical event the hook fired on (e.g. `stop`, `afterToolUse`).

hookId.description: Registered hook id that produced the message.

QueuedUserMessage.description: User message waiting for the current agent run to finish.

autoDispatch.description:
**Held** (decisions 5 & 16). When `false`, `drainMessageQueue` skips this
item entirely — it never auto-submits at idle; only an explicit human action
(release / send-now) dispatches it, starting a fresh turn tree. Absent means
a normal auto-draining queued message. Only ever `false` (never `true`) so a
"held" item is unrepresentable as auto-dispatching (execution-guidance rule
3). Set when a stale-epoch hook send-now downgrades (decision 16), and — in
C3 — when an over-budget hook message arrives.

editedByUser.description:
True once a human edits a hook-originated message (decision 10). The origin
stays `kind: 'hook'`; this records that the text no longer matches the hook's
output so the spine stays honest.

epoch.description:
Emitting turn-tree epoch (decision 16) for hook-originated items. Compared
against the thread's current turn tree to detect a stale late output; a
stale send-now downgrades to held rather than aborting an unrelated turn.

RemoteAgentLink.description:
Durable link between a cloud-agent run, the GitHub PR it produced, and the
chat thread that launched it (issue #690, Q6). Persisted on the launching
thread's `meta.json` as the source of truth; a per-project reverse index
(`agent-pr-index.jsonl`) is derived from these so the PR pane can answer
"which thread/agent owns PR #123" without scanning every thread.

`agentId` + `provider` + `createdAt` are known at launch; `runId`, `branch`,
and `repo` are recorded when available; `prUrl` is filled in once the agent's
output reveals the PR it opened (agents launch with `autoCreatePR`).

agentId.description: Provider-side agent id (Cursor agent / Anthropic managed agent).

branch.description: Local branch the run was seeded from.

prUrl.description: The PR the agent opened, once detected.

runId.description: Provider-side run/session id for the launching turn, when the API exposes one.

RemoteAgentPrIndexEntry.description: One line of a project's `agent-pr-index.jsonl` reverse index.

detail.description: Free-form model reasoning (what the prompt misses / should verify).

RoadmapIssueCoverageMatch.description: One model-judged match: open issue → existing roadmap item.

RoadmapReviewDepth.description:
Roadmap review (issue #556 follow-up): on demand, judge whether each backlog
item has been resolved using GitHub issue state (pinned + cross-linked issues),
commits, and the small-tasks model. Advisory only — verdicts are stamped on
notes for display but never auto-change status.

Bulk review (◎) scopes commits since the last *acknowledged* backlog review
(see completeRoadmapReview). Deep single-item review uses the item's full
lifetime commit window and a richer prompt.

commits.description: Oneline git log since `since` (or the latest commits when first run).

runId.description: Id for this bulk pass — stamped on each item and returned on acknowledge.

since.description: ISO timestamp of the previous acknowledged backlog review, or null.

SessionBackup.description:
A restore point for the user's pre-agent worktree. `ref` names a
`refs/copse/backups/*` commit capturing every uncommitted change (tracked and
untracked) as it was before Copse began applying edits over it. Surfaced to
the renderer so the git-changes pane can offer a one-click restore.

createdAt.description: Epoch millis when the snapshot was taken.

paths.description: Workspace-relative paths that were dirty when the backup was taken.

ShadowedAgent.description: A definition that lost a name collision, kept so Settings can explain the loss.

shadowedBy.description: Path of the definition that won.

externalLinks.description: Unique external hostnames the skill's SKILL.md references (http/https).

SkippedAgentFile.description:
A file under an `agents/` directory that did not become an agent, and why.

Surfaced in Settings rather than only logged: for the user who asked for this
feature, an agent that silently fails to appear is the worst outcome, and
"which of my six roots did this come from" is unanswerable from a console
warning they never see.

SshWorkspaceHost.description: Persisted SSH workspace host entry (`sshWorkspaceHosts` setting).

forwardAgent.description: Opt-in agent forwarding for this host (default off).

StreamChunk.description:
Everything that can flow through the app's single output stream. It is what
the agent loop emits (`AgentStreamChunk`: the provider contract plus text
rewrites, context-pressure signals, and subagent lifecycle) plus the
app-level orchestration events injected around the loop — todos, history
trimming, post-turn review, and the two-model diff comparison. The loop only
ever emits the `AgentStreamChunk` subset, so a loop stream is always
assignable to a `StreamChunk` sink.

estimated.description: Token counts are a local ~4 chars/token estimate, not agent-reported.

usageSource.description:
When set, the usage ledger records this source instead of `'agent'`.
Used for the dedicated advisor cost line (issue #566).

source.description: Present when an external agent reported the values instead of Copse estimating them.

resultFormat.description:
`'markdown'` when `result` is agent-authored Markdown (ACP tool output)
and should render through the Markdown pipeline rather than a raw `<pre>`.

issuesFound.description: Present on terminal done chunks from a structured review verdict.

createdAt.description: Wall-clock time the message was first created; absent on sessions persisted before timestamps existed.

reasoning.description: Accumulated reasoning / "thinking" text streamed before this message's content, mirroring `ChatMessage.reasoning`.

agentColor.description: `color` from the definition's frontmatter, for the card's accent.

agentName.description:
Name of the user-authored definition this run came from (`kind: 'custom'`).
The card is labelled from this — every other kind has a fixed label, but a
custom agent's identity is the whole point of showing it.

localFallback.description:
True when local subagent routing was enabled but unavailable (LM Studio
down / no model resolvable), so the run silently used the cloud parent
model. Rendered as a warning on the card — otherwise the fallback is
indistinguishable from intentional cloud routing.

model.description:
Model this subagent ran on (`lmstudio:<id>` = local). Surfaced on the card
so "did this explore actually use my local model?" is answerable per run.

archivedAt.description:
When set, the thread is archived: hidden from the sidebar and `@`-thread
catalog, but kept on disk under `~/.copse/workspace/<projectId>/<id>/`.
Soft-hide (not a delete) — restore is a later UI concern.

archives.description:
Archives (zips) the user has attached to this thread, in the order they
were sent. Read the same two ways `videos` is: `read_archive` is only
offered on threads that have one, and the paths are restated in the tool's
description every turn so trimming cannot lose them.

automation.description: Provenance for a task created by a project automation schedule.

contextTrims.description: Populated when history compaction runs during an agent turn (also in JSONL export).

continuationUsed.description:
Machine-initiated new turns already spent in the current turn tree (decision
5, C3). Counts queue-drain continuations (hook send-now, stop / subagent
follow-ups) as they auto-dispatch; when it reaches the cap
(`DEFAULT_CONTINUATION_BUDGET`), `drainMessageQueue` flips a further
machine-originated message to **held** instead of auto-submitting. Reset to 0
when a human action (typed prompt / release) starts a fresh turn tree. The
run seeds the main-process ledger with this so its in-run tighteners (ACP
unfinished-turn recovery / closeout / pre-review / remediation) share one
counter per turn tree.

currentEpoch.description:
Epoch (turn-tree id) of the current, human-initiated turn tree (decision
16). Set when a human submission / release / send-now starts a fresh turn
tree; an async hook's `queueMessage` output carries the epoch of the turn it
was emitted from, and an epoch that no longer matches this is **stale** — its
send-now downgrades to a held queued message instead of aborting an unrelated
turn. The authoritative turn-tree ledger is C3; C2 tracks the current epoch
so the staleness check (decision 16) has a reference point.

draftPrompt.description: Unsubmitted composer text; keeps blank threads visible across switches.

gitBranch.description: Git branch this thread was started on; set on first message and persisted.

messagesLoaded.description:
`false` means this thread's transcript has not been read off disk yet, so an
empty `messages` says nothing about whether the thread has any.

Load-bearing, not cosmetic. `isBlankThread` treats an empty transcript as
"new, unused thread", `pruneBlankThreads` drops those from the store, and
the autosave reconciler then deletes anything that left — so without this
flag a metadata-only load would delete a project's entire history on its
first launch. `undefined` means "loaded" (threads built in memory, and the
demo API's whole threads).

Never persisted: both `metaOf` implementations strip it before writing.

model.description: Per-thread model override; absent means "use the global default".

modelSelections.description: Ordered picker/automatic model changes, mirrored in the thread spine.

pendingMessages.description: Prompts submitted while the agent is running; drained FIFO when idle.

prRefs.description:
GitHub PRs linked from this thread, cached on its metadata.

Derived from PR links in message text plus {@link remoteAgentLink} — that
is, from exactly the transcript a metadata-only load does not read. Caching
the scrape's result here is what lets the sidebar draw its PR chip without
the transcript, and it is refreshed whenever the transcript is in memory
(on append, and on hydration).

queuePaused.description: True while a queued message is being edited; suspends FIFO draining.

reasoning.description:
Per-chat reasoning dial, set from the composer footer. Overrides the level
saved against the model in Settings for this chat's turns only, so "this
one's hard, think harder" does not permanently re-tune the model. Absent
means the model's own saved level applies.

resolvedModel.description:
The concrete model a turn's `model` selector expanded to (e.g.
`auto:…` → `gpt-5.6-terra`). Recorded at resolution time so it survives a
turn that fails before any usage, unlike the live `byModel` usage map.
Absent on threads written before this was captured.

todos.description: Structured task plan for multi-step agent work (updated via update_todos).

unreadAt.description: Latest agent completion that happened while this thread was not selected.

videos.description:
Videos the user has attached to this thread, in the order they were sent.

Recorded on send (not on chip creation), so a video attached and then
removed before sending never counts. Two things read it: `video_frames` is
only offered to the model on threads that have one, and the paths are
restated in the tool's description every turn — the reference block in the
user's message is the only other place they appear, and history trimming
can drop it out from under a long conversation.

workingBrief.description: Persisted parent/explore goal; set on the first user message in the thread.

worktreeChoice.description: Checkout decision captured once when the thread sends its first message.

ThreadCatalogHit.description:
A catalog entry with its absolute `events.jsonl` path resolved at read time
(never persisted — the on-disk catalog stays portable). Returned by the
`threads:catalog` IPC and consumed by the `@`-thread picker + steering preamble.

ThreadCheckoutPreview.description: Non-mutating policy result shown before the first message is sent.

ThreadReview.description: Verdict from the post-turn review subagent for the most recent editing turn.

issuesFound.description:
Structured signal from the review subagent (`REVIEW_JSON.issuesFound`).
Absent on older persisted reviews; when explicitly `false` the renderer
collapses the review card by default.

byModel.description: Token totals keyed by model id (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6, lmstudio:qwen).

cacheCreationTokens.description: Cumulative cache-creation tokens across the thread (subset of `inputTokens`).

cacheReadTokens.description: Cumulative cache-read tokens across the thread (subset of `inputTokens`).

ThreadWorktree.description: Durable metadata for a linked checkout owned by one thread.

path.description: Diagnostic only; main reconstructs and validates the authoritative path.

pullRequestUrl.description: PR that made this checkout eligible for space-saving retirement.

retiredAt.description: Set while the checkout is removed but its repository branch is retained.

retiredHead.description: Local HEAD verified against its upstream immediately before retirement.

upstreamRef.description: Tracking ref whose commit matched retiredHead.

editStats.description: Line add/delete counts for file edit tools (write_file, str_replace).

kind.description:
ACP tool-call `kind` (e.g. `'execute'`, `'read'`, `'search'`), carried from
an external ACP agent so its cards group and label like the built-in tools
(see `getToolGroupKey`). Absent for the built-in agent loop.

resultFormat.description:
How to render `result`. External ACP agents author their tool output as
Markdown (fenced code, lists, prose), so it renders through the same
Markdown pipeline as assistant messages instead of a raw `<pre>`. Absent
(plain text) for built-in tools, whose results are structured payloads.

argsError.description:
Set when the provider could not parse the tool-call arguments JSON (e.g. a
truncated or malformed streamed tool call). When present, `args` is not
trustworthy and the agent loop must surface an error tool result instead of
executing the tool with empty/partial args.

kind.description:
ACP tool-call `kind` (e.g. `'execute'`, `'read'`, `'search'`), carried from
an external ACP agent so the UI can recognise its shell/terminal commands
(`'execute'`) even though they don't use the built-in `run_shell` tool.
Absent for the built-in agent loop.

TranscriptAttachment.description:
A display-only attachment chip shown in a user message's transcript. The agent
receives the expanded fenced blocks in its run payload, not these — so this is
purely how the sent message renders. `paste` chips are positional: each maps,
in order, to a U+FFFC (object-replacement) placeholder in the message
`content`; `file`/`thread` chips render as a trailing row.

content.description:
Exact text snapshot represented by a text-like chip. Persisted out-of-line
in the thread store so the sent attachment remains inspectable even when a
workspace file later changes. Absent for non-text and legacy attachments.

path.description:
Where the attached file lives, for the chips that can act on it. Set by
`video` (the chip plays the recording in a preview modal) and `archive`
(the path is what the agent unpacks) — in both cases the label alone, a
bare filename, cannot find the file again after a reload. Absent for every
other kind, which are display-only.

TurnErrorDetail.description: Bounded provider/transport detail captured when a turn fails.

details.description: Distinct nested-cause or structured-data detail, when the error carried it.

TurnOutcome.description: Durable terminal record attached to the assistant message that concluded a turn.

lastEvent.description: Last meaningful provider event observed before termination.

model.description: Concrete route selected for this turn.

provider.description: Provider slug for built-in models; external agent/plugin id otherwise.

rawStopReason.description: Provider/agent stop reason before canonical normalization.

endedOn.description:
Provider event the *original* turn ended on, i.e. what the recovery
decision was made from. Distinct from {@link TurnOutcome.lastEvent}, which
is written from the host's own chunk sink and so records the recovery's
fallback message rather than anything the agent did.

UnsupportedAgentField.description:
A frontmatter field Copse parsed but does not act on yet, surfaced per row in
Settings. `reason` is user-facing copy: a field ignored silently is
indistinguishable from one Copse mishandled.

hasUnpricedCloudUsage.description: At least one cloud model in this period has usage but no known rate.

ledgerEventCount.description: Count of events in the ledger (max 90 days retained).

trackingStartedAt.description: Earliest recorded event timestamp, or null when the ledger is empty.

VideoAttachmentRef.description:
References a thread keeps to media stored beside it. Both point at the stored
copy inside the thread's `blobs/` directory; the media handling (decoding,
size caps, MIME sniffing) lives with the app, which imports these types back.

name.description: Original file name, shown on the composer chip and in the prompt note.

path.description: Absolute path of the stored copy, inside the thread's blobs directory.

localPort.description: Local end of the SSH tunnel, or the loopback port itself.

writable.description: V1 is deliberately view-only. Later phases may make this true.

VncDiscoveryHost.description: Machine whose listening ports should be checked for RFB servers.

VncNearbyServer.description: RFB service advertised on the local network through DNS-SD/Bonjour.

VncSshHostResolution.description: Network addresses currently resolved for a configured SSH machine.

WorktreeInventoryEntry.description:
One linked checkout of the project's repository, as listed in
Settings → Sources → Worktrees. Size is deliberately absent: measuring a
checkout walks its whole tree, so it is a separate on-demand call
(`worktrees:size`) that fills in after the list has rendered.

baseBranch.description: Branch the checkout was based on, when its thread metadata still records it.

changedCount.description: Uncommitted or ignored-file entries; null when the checkout could not be inspected.

lastUsedAt.description: Most recent thread write or Git activity seen for this checkout.

managed.description: Allocated by Copse under its worktrees root (vs. created outside the app).

merged.description: Branch already contained by its base branch; null when that is unknown.

path.description: Canonical top level of the linked checkout.

WorktreePackageCleanupResult.description: Preview or completed result for the package-directory cleanup action.

WorktreePackageDirectory.description: One ignored package-manager directory that can be reclaimed from a worktree.

path.description: Path relative to the checkout root, for display and confirmation.

WorktreeRemovalResult.description:
Outcome of removing one linked checkout. Blocking results are values rather
than errors: each one is a state the UI shows and offers a next step for.

WorktreeSizeResult.description: On-disk footprint of one checkout. `truncated` means the walk hit its entry budget.

WorktreeUsage.description:
The thread a linked checkout was allocated for, as far as the chat store
still knows. `linked` distinguishes a checkout the thread still points at
from one it has already let go of (thread deleted, or metadata cleared after
an earlier removal), which is what makes a worktree safe to reclaim.

running.description: An agent turn is running in this thread right now; removal is refused.

updatedAt.description: Last write to the thread — the closest thing to "when this was last used".
